text:
GitHub in Slack can cross repos. Your brief still needs a boundary.

The Oct. 15 update lets @GitHub work across repositories in one Slack or Teams conversation: investigate a bug, create an issue, or open a PR.

Less context ferrying. More actual building.

On Tech Thursday, we connected Copilot CLI to an image model through MCP. It made the batch. We still had to judge the images.

Try this: with the integration enabled, name your frontend and backend repos and ask for a read-only bug investigation. Require evidence before any edits.

Chat is becoming a work surface. Your judgment stays in the loop.

Follow Layer8Culture if you're building with AI.

text:
GitHub agentic autofix checks its fix. You still review.

Now generally available: assign an eligible default-branch code scanning alert to Copilot. It explores files, proposes a fix, reruns CodeQL and opens a draft PR for review.

The builder value is a smaller loop from alert to checked proposal. Not a promise that every bug is gone.

Try one alert in a test repo if your enterprise has enabled access. Inspect the diff and run your application tests before merging.

Requires Code Security or Advanced Security on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, admin enablement and a Copilot billing method. Uses Code Security AI Credits and Actions minutes.

AI is moving from suggestions into checked workflows. A scan isn't the whole review.

Follow Layer8Culture for practical AI builds.

Black tech creativity isn't a preset.

text:
GitHub in Slack and Teams just made cross-repo work less fragmented.

The Oct. 15 update lets @GitHub work across multiple repositories in one conversation. That includes investigating bugs, creating issues and opening pull requests.

The useful move isn't giving it everything. It's giving one task the right context.

A brief worth keeping:
1. Name the frontend and backend repositories you can access.
2. Describe one reproducible failure and the expected result.
3. Request read-only investigation first, with file paths and evidence.
4. Review the proposed next step before requesting changes.

Try this this week, where the integration is enabled: ask @GitHub to investigate one bug using both repos, make no edits, and return the evidence plus one proposed fix.

We saw the same distinction on Tech Thursday at 28:11-29:24: Copilot CLI used MCP to generate an image batch. Connected tools handled the production step. The host still judged whether the output fit the brief. That's a separate CLI example, not a demo of this Slack update.

The signal: conversations are becoming work surfaces. Scope and review are becoming builder skills.

Save this for your next cross-repo brief.

text:
GitHub in Slack can reach across repos. A useful brief tells it where to stop.

This week's Slack and Teams update lets @GitHub investigate bugs, create issues and open PRs across repositories in one conversation.

Try one scoped task with the integration enabled: name your frontend and backend repos, describe one failure, and request a read-only investigation with file evidence before edits.

Why this matters for creators: fewer manual context handoffs between the idea and the work.

On Tech Thursday, Copilot CLI used MCP to generate an image batch. The connection worked. The first images still missed the host's quality bar. Different surface, same lesson: tool access does not replace judgment.

AI conversations are becoming work surfaces. The brief is part of the build.

Follow @layer8culture for practical AI workflows.

text:
GitHub's Oct. 15 Slack and Teams update supports multi-repository work in one conversation: investigate bugs, create issues and open PRs with less context ferrying.
Try a read-only investigation across two named repos first; our Tech Thursday Copilot CLI + MCP image batch showed why connected tools still need human judgment. The shift is chat becoming workflow.
Follow Layer8Culture if you're building with AI.

AI video gets easier when the ending frame is decided first.

In the latest Tech Thursday build, we planned six stills for five connecting clips, then assembled those clips in the editor.

Not five unrelated generations. A sequence with handoffs.

A useful first experiment: keep the subject consistent, define one start frame and one end frame, and describe a single camera move. Check that transition before generating the rest.

This visual is a cinematic reconstruction of the method, not a clip from the show.

Follow @layer8culture for AI builds you can learn from.

AI video builders: which handoff breaks first?

On Tech Thursday we connected six stills into five clips. Getting a clip isn't the same as getting a sequence.

Reply with your sticking point: consistent frames or clean transitions?
